rule: Every material DECISION.md assertion cites one or more D-* claim IDs. Each ID has one evidence strength, publication-resolvable supporting anchors, a falsifier, a probe, and a gap.

claims.claim: An in-tree declarative contract layer over the current transport is the best-supported direction because four observed replication-responsibility classes occupy distinct source sites, one real receiver omission is independently source-proven, the approach adds no external runtime dependency, and it can be cut over per family.
claims.falsifier: A bounded prototype cannot represent a current family, fails to detect an omitted required site, adds more wiring than it removes, or requires an external runtime dependency.
claims.probe: Shadow-declare one bounded family, inject missing registration/receiver/replay/cleanup cases, compare parity, then remove the replaced manual path.
claims.gap: The four cited ranges do not establish payload-validation, refan, engine-wrapper or feature-state-machine sites and do not define a complete add-path or declaration universe. No contract schema, generator, prototype, schedule, or accepted upstream design exists.

claims.claim: The contract-layer choice is not evidence of a backlog-wide fix: only three ledger identities have inferred help and 45 causally unresolved outcome rows have all four option cells unknown; six envelope identities are neutral.
claims.falsifier: A validated reclassification or controlled option result produces broader demonstrated help.
claims.probe: Group the pinned 216 cells by verdict/strength and distinguish administrative envelopes from outcome rows.
claims.gap: The 2026-09-04 six-envelope intake is outside the frozen universe; unknown does not mean unhelpable.

claims.claim: Relay project licence adequacy for modification, redistribution and derived use is not established.
claims.falsifier: An applicable grant for the intended use is produced and accepted by legal review.
claims.probe: Inventory and read all conventional licence/notice paths and references in the pinned tree.
claims.gap: A grant may exist outside the pin; this is not legal advice.

claims.claim: Relay's critical native behavioral invariants are neither inspectable from corresponding source nor independently black-box qualified at the pin.
claims.falsifier: Corresponding readable implementation source or independent exact-version runtime results establish the required invariants.
claims.probe: Classify every public/static claim by evidence strength and search for source-proven or runtime-observed core behavior.
claims.gap: Static absence does not show a mechanism is false.

claims.claim: The complete Relay player package, API, wire and rule-version contract is not reproducible or stability-qualified from the public pin.
claims.falsifier: Exact player artifact provenance, reproducible build inputs, native constants, compatibility policy and mismatch tests are supplied.
claims.probe: Compare manifest/docs/version strings/checksums/build inputs and define mismatch cases.
claims.gap: No Relay binary was executed.

claims.claim: No current Relay-backed Multivoid subsystem has evidence of an implemented non-dual-authority path.
claims.falsifier: A reviewed manifest and trace show one enroller, writer, seed source and materializer for every object/state/transition in a bounded namespace.
claims.probe: Map each active ownership surface and require the other system to be disabled or disjoint.
claims.gap: This is lack of qualifying evidence, not proof that integration is impossible.

claims.claim: The prospective pilot design has objective preflight, acceptance, stop and rollback gates, but none has been executed.
claims.falsifier: A required unknown lacks a gate, or a completed independent gate packet exists.
claims.probe: Map each critical unknown and collision control to an objective pass/stop/rollback condition.
claims.gap: A plan is not runtime evidence.

claims.claim: It is not established that broad Relay migration removes more duplicated risk than it introduces.
claims.falsifier: A complete design/prototype quantifies greater risk removal with qualified behavior and bounded new failure modes.
claims.probe: Compare measured duplicated ownership removed with dependency, package, bridge, dual-stack and rollback risks.
claims.gap: No broad design, implementation or controlled result exists.

claims.claim: Upstream acceptance is unknown for every option; Relay-backed options add unresolved dependency and packaging decisions.
claims.falsifier: Pinned upstream policy, accepted design, issue, pull request or maintainer decision directly addresses the option.
claims.probe: Inspect pinned contribution, build, release and dependency-policy surfaces without maintainer contact.
claims.gap: General contribution instructions do not predict acceptance.

claims.claim: Nine Relay critical unknowns remain: licence; corresponding source/completeness; reproducible native build; supported player distribution/authenticity; API/net/schema compatibility; dependency coexistence; lawful continuity; native-C++ to Blueprint/rule integration and gameplay-pak need; upstream acceptance.
claims.falsifier: Each named item receives the evidence required by its source gate.
claims.probe: Read and preserve every Relay critical-unknown record without collapsing dimensions.
claims.gap: Future evidence can close individual items; none is assumed closed by this decision.

claims.claim: A small isolated confirmed fix proven compatible with the contract direction should not wait.
claims.falsifier: The fix changes a shared authority/identity/wire/save contract or conflicts with the selected layer.
claims.probe: Perform a diff-scoped compatibility review and exact regression test before merge.
claims.gap: No specific patch is approved by this architecture artifact.

claims.claim: Broad repetitive implementation across the whole bug backlog should wait for causal classification and the contract-layer prototype.
claims.falsifier: The backlog receives independent causal diagnoses showing unrelated isolated defects or the prototype fails its falsifier.
claims.probe: Classify each outcome and compare repetition with a bounded contract prototype before bulk implementation.
claims.gap: The frozen ledger excludes the 2026-09-04 intake.

claims.claim: Option 1 retains all current architecture, replaces only exact diagnosed feature code, adds no Relay dependency, uses per-fix tests/package updates and is locally reversible before wire/data cutover.
claims.falsifier: A class fix necessarily changes architecture-wide ownership or an external dependency.
claims.probe: Trace each concrete patch and its tests/package/data effects.
claims.gap: No set of class fixes was supplied, so total cost and replaced code are unknown.

claims.claim: Option 1 has no demonstrated help cell, and its key risk is continued repeated multi-site wiring while causal diagnoses remain sparse.
claims.falsifier: A concrete class patch changes a frozen outcome, or diagnoses show the backlog is predominantly isolated logic.
claims.probe: Test row-specific patches and aggregate only controlled outcomes.
claims.gap: No demonstrated help does not mean the option cannot help.

claims.claim: Option 2 retains transport/save/materialization ownership, replaces manual contract wiring per family after shadow parity, adds no external runtime dependency, keeps the player package Relay-free and supports per-family backout.
claims.falsifier: Implementation requires a second transport/materializer, external runtime, or non-reversible all-at-once cutover.
claims.probe: Shadow one family, compare parity, cut over one authority, remove old path, and exercise rollback.
claims.gap: Concrete schema, generated surface and cost are unknown.

claims.claim: Option 2 plausibly helps three ledger identities representing two independent verified outcomes through MATERIALIZATION and TRANSITIONS contracts; all other outcome leverage is unknown.
claims.falsifier: The declarations cannot observe/control the outcomes, or controlled root-cause evidence assigns another class.
claims.probe: Prototype narrow postconditions against the exact verified content-view and paired-presentation outcomes.
claims.gap: No contract layer was run; the help cells remain inferred.

claims.claim: Option 2 risks abstraction mismatch, temporary dual paths and broad review cost; upstream acceptance and implementation cost remain unknown, and prototype failure would make the choice wrong.
claims.falsifier: A prototype fails coverage/omission/parity/backout gates or diagnoses show no repeated contract burden.
claims.probe: Run the bounded prototype and review a concrete upstream design.
claims.gap: No prototype or maintainer decision exists.

claims.claim: Option 3 retains Multivoid broadly, gives one disjoint target to Relay after qualification, and adds mandatory Relay player artifacts, a rule profile and an unresolved bridge/package surface.
claims.falsifier: A genuine Relay pilot requires none of those player artifacts/rules/bridge boundaries.
claims.probe: Inventory the complete exact pilot dependency and ensure the target namespace is disjoint.
claims.gap: Bridge and gameplay-pak needs remain unknown.

claims.claim: Option 3 has no demonstrated bug-help cell and carries licence, opaque behavior, version, dual-stack, coexistence and upstream unknowns.
claims.falsifier: Exact-version pilot results demonstrate row-specific help and close every applicable gate.
claims.probe: Execute only the authorized gate plan with independent review.
claims.gap: No pilot was run; no impossibility is claimed.

claims.claim: Option 3 must proceed from preflight through a disjoint canary, mismatch/non-dual/behavior/performance gates and Relay-free rollback; failure of a required gate makes it the wrong current choice.
claims.falsifier: All gates pass and the qualified benefit exceeds the in-tree alternative's result.
claims.probe: Apply G01-G17 in PILOT-DESIGN.md and promote only exact passed behavior.
claims.gap: Plan execution and authorized environment are outside this audit.

claims.claim: Option 4 would retain gameplay/save integration not supplied by Relay, broadly replace transport/replication ownership, add mandatory opaque player artifacts and cross-peer version/rule lockstep, and cross wire/authority/persistence rollback boundaries.
claims.falsifier: A complete broad design demonstrates a smaller source-reproducible surface without those retained responsibilities or cutover boundaries.
claims.probe: Map each Multivoid owner to Relay's documented inclusion/exclusion and package contract.
claims.gap: No broad design or buildable diff exists.

claims.claim: Option 4 has no demonstrated bug-help cell and no evidence that its migration risk is favourable.
claims.falsifier: Qualified broad evidence demonstrates row-specific help and net risk reduction.
claims.probe: Run representative migration and failure tests only after prerequisites close.
claims.gap: Unknown help is not no possible help.

claims.claim: Option 4 would require staged ownership replacement, full regression/mismatch/save/rejoin/load tests and converter-backed rollback; any unresolved broad-decision gate makes it the wrong current choice.
claims.falsifier: Every decision-rule prerequisite closes and a representative migration passes acceptance and reverse conversion.
claims.probe: Evaluate all eight broad-decision gates and exercise forward/back conversion before expansion.
claims.gap: None of the migration artifacts or runtime results exists.

claims.claim: Multivoid clients write a validated host save to an ephemeral slot, invoke the native save boot path, then signal world-ready; save-created actors are bound/adopted, and stable keys, actor expressions, EIDs, peers and per-player inventory ownership remain distinct implementation domains.
claims.falsifier: The pinned client world is instead wholly created from a server-owned element tree.
claims.probe: Trace save transfer/load, ready edge, actor binding and identity maps.
claims.gap: Native game loader internals and every entity family are not covered.

lineage.round_1_factual_core: Clients use native save load and bind/adopt save-created actors.
new_or_expanded_clauses: Host save bytes are validated before being written.
The client write target is an ephemeral slot.
Native save boot precedes the client world-ready signal.
Stable authored/save keys, transient actor expressions, session EIDs and peer identity are distinct identity domains.
Per-player inventory/save ownership is a fifth ownership domain rather than an object identity.
lineage.support_boundary: Each new or expanded clause is covered by the direct pinned ranges in this D-024 record; the architecture conclusion remains separately downgraded to INFERRED D-029.

claims.claim: A viable Multivoid model must preserve hybrid bind/adopt/materialize behavior and keep its identity and ownership domains independent.
claims.falsifier: A concrete alternative preserves native-save boot, materialization and every named identity/ownership distinction without a hybrid boundary or independent contracts.
claims.probe: Apply the ten-axis model to the pinned session, save, element, lifecycle and inventory paths.
claims.gap: This is an architecture judgment; it does not select a schema syntax or generator.

claims.claim: MTA concepts transfer only with adaptation: its identity indirection and server-driven initial data stream are useful references, while its server-created root/resource tree is not a direct model for VotV native-save boot.
claims.falsifier: A direct transplantation preserves native-save identity/materialization and ownership without adaptation.
claims.probe: Compare pinned MTA element/resource lifecycles to Multivoid save and actor binding.
claims.gap: MTA is a conceptual reference, not an implementation dependency.

claims.claim: The migration-analysis chat scope and pilot-design disjoint-canary scope answer different questions; the canary is selected first, while chat remains a later candidate after publication-resolvable wire-test evidence is supplied.
claims.falsifier: Chat is proven fully isolated and better covers the first qualification controls, or a canary cannot cover them.
claims.probe: Compare scope, existing test surface and non-dual coverage.
claims.gap: The exact migration-unit membership and chat wire-test search record are not in the artifact set; neither target was implemented or run.

claims.claim: The overlap analysis's current non-certification and the pilot design's prospective certification plan are retained as distinct temporal findings.
claims.falsifier: A passed certificate already exists or the plan contains no non-dual gate.
claims.probe: Compare present evidence with prospective gate semantics without averaging them.
claims.gap: No gate result exists.

claims.claim: The prior rejection's claim-strength findings are closed by the 54-row corrected matrix, downgraded cells, removal of invented Drive Box declarations, replacement of defective citations and explicit preservation of the open six-envelope scope limit.
claims.falsifier: Any rejected claim/citation is reused, a frozen identity is absent/duplicated, or the scope limit is described as closed.
claims.probe: Check each restated correction item in the publication-contained closure record against current documents and mechanically compare row identities.
claims.gap: The six 2026-09-04 capture envelopes remain open pending an addendum.
